      };
    }, () => terminalQueryRefusal({ scope: null, store: null, closed: closed ? unavailable() : null, session: sessionDead ? unavailable() : null, changes: changesStopped, partition: partitionDenied, inherited: null }), aborter.signal),
    observe<A, R>(op: Query<A, R>, args: A, options?: ObserveOptions): Observed<R> {
      const keep = options?.keep;
      const key = observationKey(op, args, options);
      return observeWatch(watches, key,
        () => Object.assign(localWatch(keep, op as Query<unknown, unknown>, args, key, incarnation, pendingRead), { opaque: () => !backend?.programs.some(p => p.name === op.name && !p.native) }),
        watch => {
          watchEphemeral(watch); const d = watch.deadlines;
          // @ref LLP 3000.023#3.4 — resubscription resumes the displayed row's original deadlines.
          if (d) scheduleExpiry(watch, d.device, d.server, d.localWakeup, d.valueDevice, d.valueServer);

    scheduleRefresh();

    current: () => { const revision = credentialRevision, epoch = incarnation; return () => revision === credentialRevision && epoch === incarnation; },
    inputsCurrent: () => answers.inputsCurrent(), unavailable: () => !!unavailable() || !!partitionDenied || link !== "online",
    refreshing: () => !!refreshing, pending: pendingRead, intents: followingIntents,
    send: (op, args, body, signal) => post(`/following/${op.name}`, { ...body, args }, undefined, undefined, false, undefined, undefined, signal),
  });
  progress.bind(client); readWork.bind(client, watches);
  bindWatchPeek(client, watches, unavailable);
  trackRotation(client, () => refreshing);
  trackClose(client, closingResponses);
  if (!deferStart(options, start)) await start();
  stopHost = core.onClient?.(client, base);
  bindSessionRefusal(client, () => authRefusal);
  release = servedRelease({ url: base, fetch: doFetch, headers: () => requestCredentials().headers, current: () => !closed && !sessionDead && !partitionDenied && !versionBlocked() });
  Object.assign(client, { release });
  client.onSession(() => release?.invalidate());
  client.onViewer(() => release?.invalidate());
  return client;
  } catch (error) {
    stopSuspend?.(); stopOutbox?.();
    stopClock?.(); stopSessionTiming();
    await deliveryQueue?.stop();
    aborter.abort();
    // This constructor owns the opened device until return; startup failures release it.
    try { await media?.close(); await core.close(); } catch {}
    throw error;
  }
}

/** Device-less identity apps need explicit session persistence. TypeScript cannot

function problem(error: unknown): Refusal {
  if (error instanceof DeviceVersionError) return error.why;
  if ((error as { why?: Refusal })?.why?.code.startsWith("E_READ_ONLY")) return (error as { why: Refusal }).why;
  if (error instanceof StorageWarning) return error.why;
  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
  const code = message.includes("E_AUTH:") ? "E_AUTH" : "E_CLIENT";
  return { code, family: code === "E_AUTH" ? "auth" : "client", message,
    site: "app.auth", rewrite: "await app.auth.login(email, password)" };
}

// A restored snapshot lost its compare-and-save race to another app. Opening
// must retry from storage without revoking the winning session's family.
class RestorationChanged extends Error {}
class SessionEpochChanged extends StorageWarning {
  constructor() { super({ code: "E_AUTH", family: "auth", message: "the stored session changed in another app", site: "app.auth", rewrite: "await app.auth.login(email, password)" }); }
}

/** A configuration refusal is an observable app, before any identity or storage
 * is opened. Keeping its client fenced also prevents accidental public reads. */
function refusedApp(options: AppOptions, why: Refusal): App {
  const raw = sdkOwned(() => createClient({ url: options.url, readOnly: options.readOnly ?? false,
    fetch: async () => Response.json({ denied: why }, { status: 403 }) }));
  const client = guardClient(raw, async () => false, () => false, () => why).client;
  bindSessionRefusal(client, () => why);
  const result = { ok: false, why } as const;
  const snapshot: AuthSnapshot = { state: "signed-out", viewer: null, why };
  const refused = () => Promise.resolve(result);
  const auth: AppAuth = { ...snapshot, getSnapshot: () => snapshot, onChange: () => () => {},
    signup: refused, login: refused, guest: refused, logout: refused, logoutEverywhere: refused };
  return { client, online: onlineView(client), onOnlineChange: () => () => {}, auth,
    ready: Promise.resolve(result), mutate: client.mutate, close: () => client.close() };
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — proof custody stays outside authored screens.
export function createApp(options: AppOptions): App {
  const app = createAppInner(options);
  // The proof driver installs this callback before page scripts. Ordinary
  // applications neither import the witness nor publish an app global.
  if (typeof window !== "undefined" && typeof window.location?.search === "string" && new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("witness") === "web") {
    const observer = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window, Symbol.for("snapback4.proof.app"));
    if (observer?.writable === false && observer.configurable === false && typeof observer.value === "function") observer.value(app);
  }
  return app;
}

function createAppInner(options: AppOptions): App {
  validateReadOptions(options);
  // @ref LLP 3000.013.000#17 — refuse unwritable configuration before identity branching.
  if (options.writes !== undefined && (options.writes !== "online" || options.device || options.readOnly)) {
    return refusedApp(options, { code: "E_CLIENT", family: "client", site: "createApp.writes",
      message: options.writes !== "online" ? 'writes must be "online" or omitted'
        : 'writes: "online" cannot be combined with a device or readOnly',
      rewrite: 'omit writes with a device/readOnly, or createApp({ url, writes: "online" })' });

      throw new StorageWarning(admissionRefusal("a persona browser journal needs IndexedDB storage", "createApp.persona", "omit sessionStore, or pass localStorageSessionStore()"));
    if (options.persona === undefined && (!options.sessionStore || !(sessionReader(options.sessionStore) && sessionAuthority(options.sessionStore))))
      throw new StorageWarning(admissionRefusal("this browser app needs sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore() for device-less writes", "createApp", ONLINE_WRITE_FIX));
  }

  let assets: AssetRetention | undefined, configurationError: StorageWarning | undefined;

  catch (error) {
    configurationError = new StorageWarning({ code: "E_CLIENT", family: "client", message: String(error),
      site: "app.assets", rewrite: 'createApp({ url, device, assets: { keep: "viewed", maxBytes: 67108864 } })' });
  }
  const url = options.url.replace(/\/$/, "");

  const fetcher = clock.wrap(options.fetch ?? defaultFetch);

  const persist = <T>(work: () => Promise<T>) => {

  // I1: every revocation compares the stored bearer. I2/I5: one record
  // commits session + epoch, only after opening succeeds. I3: journal before
  // displacement, drain after commit. I4: an observed epoch fences old work.
  // I6: hide the public view before client retirement can notify observers.
  // I7: known refusal conditionally tombstones its bearer before later opens;
  // its consumed predecessor is also refused; unrelated successors are preserved.
  // I8: hiding permanently fences exposed facades; raw retry custody is private.
  // I9: global logout fences a principal/generation; a late rotation inherits
  // that obligation. Only a successful logout-all acknowledges global removal.

  const removeSession = (expectedToken?: string | readonly string[], restoring = false, global?: { session: Session; epoch: string; consumed?: string | undefined }, explicitLogout = false) => persist(() => storeLock(custodyKey, async () => {
    const commit = async () => {
      const text = await storage.get(custodyKey);
      let token: string | undefined, kept: Session | undefined;
      try { kept = text ? JSON.parse(text) : undefined; if (typeof kept?.token === "string") token = kept.token; } catch {}
      // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.4 — logout owns this principal in every epoch,
      // including peer rotations. Read after any already-admitted session commit
      // finishes; only a different principal's replacement is protected.
      if (explicitLogout && lastOwned && kept?.token && kept.principal !== lastOwned.principal) {
        // Preserve this account's token and epoch while fencing an older user's
        // sign-in responses. The watermark travels with later session commits.
        const prior = signOuts(text);
        await storage.set(custodyKey, JSON.stringify({ ...kept,
          snapback4SignOuts: { ...prior, [lastOwned.principal]: (prior[lastOwned.principal] ?? 0) + 1 } }));
        return;
      }
      // Choose under the same lock as the fence. A peer may have saved a
      // successor; our raw client may instead own a newer, unpersisted one.
      if (global && token && kept?.principal !== global.session.principal) throw new SessionEpochChanged();
      if (global) {
        // Already inside the session lock: read directly, without reentering
        // retirement's lock. Completed fences survive in the journal after a
        // new login removes the tombstone. Only this principal's fences count.
        const fences = mergeFences(revocations.fences(text),
          revocations.journalFences(await storage.get(custodyKey + ".revocations")));
        if (fences.some(value => value.principal === global.session.principal && BigInt(value.epoch) > BigInt(global.epoch))) throw new SessionEpochChanged();
        // A replacement can also commit while this operation waits for its
        // rotation. Compare that session's committed scope, not readEpoch's
        // shared/legacy counter, which can advance for another principal.
        if (token && BigInt(sessionEpoch(text) ?? "0") > BigInt(global.epoch)) throw new SessionEpochChanged();
      }
      const globalToken = global ? (token && token !== global.consumed ? token : global.session.token) : undefined;
      if (expectedToken !== undefined && !(typeof expectedToken === "string" ? [expectedToken] : expectedToken).includes(token ?? "")) {
        if (restoring) throw new RestorationChanged();
        return;
      }
      const currentEpoch = await readEpoch();
      const epoch = (BigInt(currentEpoch) + 1n).toString();
      // The tombstone is the single durable logout commit. It carries retirement
      // custody too, so a quota failure cannot split the fence from the bearer.
      const retired = revocations.embedded(text);
      const all = [...new Set([...revocations.global(text), ...(globalToken ? [globalToken] : [])])];
      const fences = mergeFences(revocations.fences(text), global && globalToken ? [{ principal: global.session.principal, epoch, tokens: [globalToken] }] : []);
      await storage.set(custodyKey, JSON.stringify({ snapback4Logout: epoch, snapback4Backend: url,
        snapback4Retired: [...new Set([...retired, ...revocations.pending(), ...(token ? [token] : [])])].filter(token => !all.includes(token)),
        ...(all.length ? { snapback4LogoutAll: all } : {}), ...(fences.length ? { snapback4GlobalFences: fences } : {}) }));
    };
    try { await commit(); }
    catch (error) {
      // A known server refusal cannot be treated as a recoverable session.
      // Retry one failed storage operation while retaining the same lock; a
      // second failure is reported and must never authorize local data access.
      if (expectedToken === undefined || global || error instanceof RestorationChanged) throw error;
      await commit();
    }
  }));
  const sessionStore: SessionStore = {
    get: key => persist(() => storeLock(key, () => storage.get(key))),
    set: (key, value) => persist(() => storeLock(key, () => storage.set(key, value))),
    delete: key => key === custodyKey ? removeSession() : persist(() => storeLock(key, () => storage.delete(key))),

  async function restore() {
    let bytes: string | null = null, epoch = "0";
    const restoringStore: SessionStore = {
      ...sessionStore,
      get: key => persist(() => storeLock(key, async () => {
        epoch = await openingEpoch();
        bytes = await storage.get(key);
        return bytes;
      })),
      // Invalid/expired data is garbage collection, not an explicit logout.
      // Compare the exact snapshot; a replacement makes restoration restart.
      delete: key => persist(() => storeLock(key, async () => {
        if (await storage.get(key) !== bytes) throw new RestorationChanged();
        const keptEpoch = sessionEpoch(bytes);
        if (keptEpoch !== null) await storage.set(key, JSON.stringify({ snapback4Logout: keptEpoch,
          ...(Object.keys(signOuts(bytes)).length ? { snapback4SignOuts: signOuts(bytes) } : {}) }));
        else await storage.delete(key);
      })),
    };
    // Keep structurally valid bytes until expired metadata has had one chance
    // to obtain authoritative staging evidence. Production/offline expiry still
    // refuses, and cleanup remains conditional on this exact custody snapshot.
    let session = await restoreSession(url, restoringStore, () => 0, readOnly);
    if (session && !options.device && session.expiresAt <= clock.issuedDeviceNow()) {
      session = await restoreStagingTiming(url, session, options.fetch ?? defaultFetch);
      if (!session) await restoringStore.delete(custodyKey);
    }
    return { session, epoch };
  }

  type Scope = { cleanup?: { depth: number; client?: Client; finish(): void }; online?: ReturnType<typeof ownOnline>; openOnline?: () => void; valid: boolean; sealing?: boolean; waitRotation?: () => Promise<void>; epoch: string; session: Session; consumed?: string | undefined; issued: Set<string>; aborter: AbortController; client?: Client; view?: Client; expose?: () => Client; fenceView?: () => () => void; save?: () => Promise<void>; logout?: Promise<void>; stop(): void; pause(): void };

  const enqueue = <T>(work: () => Promise<T>) => {
    const result = operations.catch(() => {}).then(work);
    operations = result;
    return result;

  const inactive = (): Extract<SignIn, { ok: false }> => ({ ok: false, why: { code: "E_CLOSED", family: "client", message: "this app operation was superseded", site: "app.auth", rewrite: "await app.auth.login(email, password)" } });
  const hide = (state: AuthState = "signed-out", pause = true, why?: Refusal) => {
    if (pause) owner?.pause();
    const notifyHidden = [...scopes].map(scope => scope.fenceView?.());
    if (current !== owner?.view) void current.close();
    current = anonymous(why);
    signedOutOnline = onlineView(current);
    publish(closed ? "signed-out" : state, null, why);
    for (const notify of notifyHidden) notify?.();

  // @ref LLP 3000.013#6 — a scope retains already-dispatched responses
  // through its local credential cleanup, including implicit retirement.
  async function cleanupScope<T>(scope: Scope, work: () => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    const capture = scope.cleanup ??= { depth: 0, finish() {} };
    // Preparation can schedule credential work before a Client exists. A
    // later task attaches its raw/custody owner to that same cleanup lifetime.
    if (scope.client && capture.client !== scope.client) {
      const prior = capture.finish, finish = holdClose(scope.client);
      capture.client = scope.client;
      capture.finish = () => { prior(); finish(); };
    }
    capture.depth++;
    try { return await work(); }
    finally {
      await scope.logout?.catch(() => {});
      await persistence.catch(() => {});
      if (--capture.depth === 0) {
        if (scope.cleanup === capture) delete scope.cleanup;
        capture.finish();
      }
    }
  }
  async function release() {
    const previous = owner;
    owner = undefined;
    if (!previous) return;
    await cleanupScope(previous, async () => {
      previous.pause();
      try { await previous.client.close(); }
      finally {
        if (previous.valid) try { await previous.save?.(); } catch (error) { report(error); }
        const retired = previous.client.session()?.token;
        previous.stop(); await persistence.catch(() => {}); previous.valid = false; scopes.delete(previous);
        if (retired) previous.issued.add(retired);
        for (const token of previous.issued) revokeRetired(token, { principal: previous.session.principal, epoch: previous.epoch });
      }
    });
  }
  function observeEpoch(epoch: string) {
    // A provisional owner does not replace the rollback candidate's duty to
    // observe the shared epoch. Fence every older scope before any callback.
    fenceScopes([...scopes].filter(scope => scope.valid && BigInt(epoch) > BigInt(scope.epoch)), new SessionEpochChanged());
  }
  function fence(scope: Scope, error: SessionEpochChanged) {
    fenceScopes([scope], error);
  }
  function fenceScopes(stale: Scope[], error: SessionEpochChanged) {
    for (const scope of stale) scope.valid = false;
    const affected = owner && stale.includes(owner) ? owner : undefined;
    const expected = revision;
    // Publish before raw retirement emits client callbacks, with every rollback
    // candidate already invalid. Auth and client observers share this boundary.
    if (affected && !closed) hide("restoring");
    for (const scope of stale) void cleanupScope(scope, () => {
      scope.pause(); scope.stop(); scope.aborter.abort();
      return scope.client?.signOut();
    }).catch(() => {});
    if (!affected || closed) return;
    void enqueue(async () => {
      if (owner !== affected) return;
      await release();
      if (revision === expected) publish("signed-out", null, error.why);
    }).catch(report);
  }
  async function open(session: Session, expected: number, epoch: string, restoring = false, openingSignOuts?: Record<string, number>): Promise<SignIn> {
    if (closed || revision !== expected) { revokeRetired(session.token); return inactive(); }
    const previous = owner, previousVisible = snapshot.state === "signed-in";
    hide("restoring", false);
    // Keep the prior runtime's rotations and pending-write custody alive until
    // commit. A failed replacement must not repair, revoke or detach it.
    // Every opener owns its persistence, including before it returns a Client.
    // Logout invalidates this guard synchronously, ahead of any network work.
    const scope: Scope = { valid: true, epoch, session, issued: new Set([session.token]), aborter: new AbortController(), stop() {}, pause() {} };
    const retire = (token: string) => revokeRetired(token, { principal: session.principal, epoch: scope.epoch });
    const cancelled = (): SignIn => {
      // A peer can fence this provisional scope before it becomes owner.
      // The still-current auth operation must finish cleanup/publication (or
      // retry restoration), rather than return with its view left restoring.
      if (!scope.valid && !closed && revision === expected) throw restoring ? new RestorationChanged() : new SessionEpochChanged();
      return inactive();
    };
    scopes.add(scope);
    if (options.device) refuseReadDevice(session);
    let restoreToken = restoring ? session.token : undefined;
    let preparing = true, committing = false;
    const scopedStore: SessionStore = {
      get: sessionStore.get,
      set: (key, value) => cleanupScope(scope, () => persist(() => storeLock(key, async () => {
        if (key !== custodyKey) { await storage.set(key, value); return; }
        const next = JSON.parse(value) as Session;
        const saved = await storage.get(key);
        let kept: Session | undefined;
        try { kept = saved ? JSON.parse(saved) : undefined; } catch {}
        if (!scope.valid || await readEpoch() !== epoch || (openingSignOuts &&
          (signOuts(saved)[session.principal] ?? 0) !== (openingSignOuts[session.principal] ?? 0))) {
          retire(next.token);
          const error = new SessionEpochChanged(); fence(scope, error);
          throw restoreToken !== undefined ? new RestorationChanged() : error;
        }
        if (restoreToken !== undefined && kept?.token !== restoreToken) {
          if (next.token !== scope.session.token && next.token !== kept?.token) retire(next.token);
          throw new RestorationChanged();
        }
        // Constructors can write/rotate several times. These saves are private
        // until their final successful opening; no durable account is displaced.
        if (preparing && !committing) { scope.session = next; return; }
        const replacing = preparing && !restoring;
        if (!replacing && kept?.token && kept.token !== scope.session.token && kept?.token !== next.token) {
          retire(next.token);
          const error = new SessionEpochChanged(); fence(scope, error);
          throw restoreToken !== undefined ? new RestorationChanged() : error;
        }
        if (replacing) await revocations.stage([...(kept?.token ? [kept.token] : []), ...revocations.pending()].filter(token => token !== next.token));
        const nextEpoch = replacing && kept?.token && kept.token !== next.token ? (BigInt(epoch) + 1n).toString() : epoch;
        // I2/I5: no separate epoch write and no fallible opening after this set.
        // Advancing the epoch already fences every opener that captured these
        // watermarks. Same-epoch rotations must keep their principal fences.
        if (kept?.token !== next.token || replacing || kept?.expiresAt !== next.expiresAt || kept?.capExpiresAt !== next.capExpiresAt) await storage.set(key, JSON.stringify({ ...next, snapback4Epoch: nextEpoch, snapback4Backend: url,
          ...(nextEpoch === epoch && Object.keys(signOuts(saved)).length ? { snapback4SignOuts: signOuts(saved) } : {}) }));
        lastOwned = { principal: next.principal, epoch: nextEpoch };
        epoch = nextEpoch; scope.epoch = nextEpoch; scope.session = next; scope.consumed = undefined;
        scope.issued.clear(); scope.issued.add(next.token);
        if (restoreToken !== undefined) restoreToken = next.token;
      }))),
      delete: key => scope.valid ? cleanupScope(scope, () => key === custodyKey ? removeSession(scope.session.token, restoreToken !== undefined) : sessionStore.delete(key)) : Promise.resolve(),
    };
    let pendingAuthority: Promise<boolean> | undefined;
    function authorized(): Promise<boolean> {
      // Memory/native session stores keep their original scheduling: their
      // persistence queue can contain an admitted write held by its owner.
      if (!authority || preparing) return checkAuthority();
      // Calls queued before this read starts share one linearization point.
      // Clear before acquiring the lock: calls arriving during/after the read
      // always queue a new committed transaction, including after peer logout.
      if (pendingAuthority) return pendingAuthority;
      return pendingAuthority = checkAuthority(() => { pendingAuthority = undefined; });
    }
    async function checkAuthority(start?: () => void): Promise<boolean> {
      const valid = await persist(() => {
        start?.();
        return storeLock(custodyKey, async () => {
          if (!scope.valid) return false;
          if (preparing || !authority) {
            if (await readEpoch() !== epoch) return false;
            if (preparing || !readOnly) return true;
            const bytes = await storage.get(custodyKey);
            const saved = bytes ? JSON.parse(bytes) as Session : undefined;
            return !!saved?.token && saved.principal === scope.session.principal;
          }
          const { marker, raw } = await authority.readScope(custodyKey);
          const stored = sessionEpoch(raw) ?? "0", legacy = marker ?? "0";
          const current = BigInt(legacy) > BigInt(stored) ? legacy : stored;
          observeEpoch(current);
          if (!scope.valid || current !== epoch) return false;
          if (!raw || logoutEpoch(raw) !== null) return false;
          try { return JSON.parse(raw)?.principal === scope.session.principal; } catch { return false; }
        });
      });
      if (!valid) { fence(scope, new SessionEpochChanged()); return false; }
      return true;
    }
    function admit(): Refusal | undefined {
      if (!options.device) {
        const refused = onlineWritesRefusal();
        if (refused) return refused;
      }
      const read = sessionReader(backing);
      if (!read) return admissionRefusal("the session store cannot be checked synchronously", "app.mutate", "use localStorageSessionStore() on the web, then retry with the same id");
      try {
        const marker = read(epochKey) ?? "0";
        const raw = read(custodyKey);
        const stored = sessionEpoch(raw) ?? "0";
        const currentEpoch = BigInt(marker) > BigInt(stored) ? marker : stored;
        // An unlocked observation may catch our own session commit before its
        // in-memory epoch assignment. Confirm under the lock before fencing.
        if (!scope.valid || !raw || logoutEpoch(raw) !== null || JSON.parse(raw)?.principal !== scope.session.principal || currentEpoch !== epoch) {
          void authorized().catch(() => {});
          return new SessionEpochChanged().why;
        }
      } catch (error) { return admissionRefusal(`session storage is unavailable: ${String(error)}`, "app.mutate"); }
      return undefined;
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.013.000#3 — a device-less browser app journals writes when the
    // backend syncs no table, or when the app chose writes: "online".
    type WritesDecision = { mode: "journal" } | { mode: "synced"; tables: string[] } | { mode: "unknown"; why: string };
    let writesDecision: WritesDecision = { mode: "unknown", why: "the backend's schema has not been read" };
    let readingWrites: Promise<void> | undefined, lastWritesRead = 0;
    const journalSupport = !options.device && !readOnly && browserAdmission() && !!sessionReader(backing) && !!authority && !!globalThis.navigator?.locks;
    const readWrites = (): Promise<void> => readingWrites ??= (async () => {
      lastWritesRead = Date.now();
      let next: WritesDecision;
      try {
        const token = raw?.session()?.token ?? scope.session.token;
        const response = await scopedFetch(url + "/schema", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
        const json = await response.json() as { schema?: { tables?: Record<string, { sync?: unknown } | null> }; denied?: Refusal };
        const tables = json?.schema?.tables;
        const declaration = (table: unknown) => !!table && typeof table === "object" && !Array.isArray(table);
        // A malformed reply is an unknown decision, never "nothing syncs".
        if (!response.ok || !declaration(tables) || !Object.values(tables!).every(declaration)) next = { mode: "unknown", why: json?.denied?.message ?? `GET /schema answered ${response.status} without a table map` };
        else {
          const synced = Object.entries(tables!).filter(([, table]) => table?.sync).map(([name]) => name).sort();
          next = synced.length ? { mode: "synced", tables: synced } : { mode: "journal" };
        }
      } catch (error) { next = { mode: "unknown", why: String(error) }; }
      if (writesDecision.mode === "unknown") writesDecision = next;
    })().finally(() => { readingWrites = undefined; });
    function onlineWritesRefusal(): Refusal | undefined {
      if (!sessionReader(backing) || !authority) return admissionRefusal("this browser app has no device, and its session store is not localStorageSessionStore(): the browser write journal needs its synchronous reader and IndexedDB authority", "app.mutate", ONLINE_WRITE_FIX);
      if (!globalThis.navigator?.locks) return admissionRefusal("this browser has no Web Locks (navigator.locks); the browser write journal cannot serialize tabs", "app.mutate", "use a browser with Web Locks, or " + BROWSER_WRITE_FIX);
      if (writesDecision.mode === "synced") return admissionRefusal(`this schema syncs ${writesDecision.tables.join(", ")}; a browser app without a device journals writes only when no table syncs`, "app.mutate",
        `${BROWSER_WRITE_FIX} for offline reads, or createApp({ url, sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore(), writes: "online" }) to write through the server only`);
      if (writesDecision.mode === "unknown") {
        if (Date.now() - lastWritesRead >= 5_000) void readWrites().catch(() => {});
        return { ...admissionRefusal(`the backend has not said whether its tables sync, so the browser write journal is not chosen yet (${writesDecision.why})`, "app.mutate",
          'retry with the same id once the backend answers, or pass writes: "online"'), retryable: true };
      }
      return undefined;
    }
    const scopedRequest = async (input: Parameters<typeof fetch>[0], init?: Parameters<typeof fetch>[1], currentArm?: () => boolean): Promise<Response> => {
      // Cancel backend acquisition before a local Client exists. Once open,
      // the client owns cancellation and late rotation revocation itself.
      const path = new URL(typeof input === "string" || input instanceof URL ? input : input.url).pathname;
      if (path === new URL(url + "/auth/logout").pathname) {
        const headers = new Headers(init?.headers ?? (typeof input === "string" || input instanceof URL ? undefined : input.headers));
        const token = headers.get("authorization")?.match(/^Bearer (.+)$/i)?.[1];
        await scope.logout?.catch(() => {});
        if (token) await revocations.retire(token, { principal: session.principal, epoch: scope.epoch });
        return Response.json({ ok: true });
      }
      if (scope.sealing && path === new URL(url + "/auth/refresh").pathname) throw new Error("global logout is selecting its retry credential");
      if (!await authorized()) return Response.json({ denied: new SessionEpochChanged().why }, { status: 401 });
      const retiredArm = armRefusal(requestArm(init));
      if (retiredArm) return Response.json({ denied: retiredArm }, { status: 401 });
      if (currentArm && !currentArm()) return Response.json({ denied: new SessionEpochChanged().why }, { status: 401 });
      // The epoch check awaits storage. A concurrent response can retire this
      // store while it waits; never dispatch a fresh request through that gap.
      if (changedStore && !path.startsWith("/auth/")) return Response.json({ denied: changedStore });
      if (init?.signal?.aborted) throw init.signal.reason ?? new Error("request was cancelled");
      if (!scope.valid && !path.startsWith("/auth/")) throw new Error("app opener was cancelled");
      if (path !== "/schema") {
        const response = await fetcher(input, init);
        if (path === new URL(url + "/auth/refresh").pathname) {
          try {
            const issued = (await response.clone().json() as { session?: Session }).session;
            if (issued?.token) {
              scope.issued.add(issued.token);
              // Record only the known consumed kept predecessor, not arbitrary
              // tokens from a failed save or another runtime's successor.
              const prior = new Headers(init?.headers).get("authorization")?.slice(7);
              if (issued.principal === scope.session.principal && prior === scope.session.token) scope.consumed = prior;

}

import type { Refusal, Write } from "./contract.ts";

// @ref LLP 3000.013#6 — each invocation owns its reply through the public close cutoff.
// The private app wrapper can extend that cutoff through its session cleanup;
// raw close still waits only for its own local work, never for caller outcomes.
const owners = new WeakMap<object, ClosingResponses>();
export const trackClose = (client: object, responses: ClosingResponses): void => { owners.set(client, responses); };
export const inheritClose = (client: object, raw: object): void => {
  const responses = owners.get(raw); if (responses) owners.set(client, responses);
};
export const holdClose = (client?: object): (() => void) => client ? owners.get(client)?.hold() ?? (() => {}) : () => {};

export class ClosingResponses {
  private phase: "open" | "closing" | "complete" = "open";
  private finished = false;
  private holds = 0;
  private resolve!: () => void;
  readonly done = new Promise<void>(resolve => { this.resolve = resolve; });
  begin(): void { if (this.phase === "open") this.phase = "closing"; }
  hold(): () => void {
    if (this.phase === "complete") return () => {};
    this.holds++;
    let held = true;
    return () => { if (held) { held = false; this.holds--; this.complete(); } };
  }
  finish(): void { this.finished = true; this.complete(); }
  private complete(): void {
    if (this.finished && this.holds === 0 && this.phase !== "complete") { this.phase = "complete"; this.resolve(); }
  }
  // A body can become known while open, then cross close during receipt
  // application. The invocation retains it from dispatch through the cutoff.
  request(): ClosingResponse { return new ClosingResponse(() => this.phase !== "complete"); }
}

/** A request's identity is this object, never its mutation/action id. Retrying
 * the transport may reuse it; overlapping submissions cannot steal its body. */
export class ClosingResponse {
  private json?: Record<string, unknown>;
  constructor(private capturing: () => boolean) {}
  capture(json: Record<string, unknown>, status: number): void {
    if (this.capturing() && status < 500) this.json = json;
  }
  take(): { ok: true; json: Record<string, unknown> } | undefined {
    return this.json ? { ok: true, json: this.json } : undefined;
  }
  write<R>(pending: Write<R>): Write<R> {
    if (pending.state !== "pending") return pending;
    const json = this.json;
    if (json?.state === "sent") return { state: "sent", id: pending.id, seq: Number(json.seq ?? 0),
      ...(json.replayed === true ? { replayed: true } : { result: json.result as R }) };
    const why = (json?.why ?? json?.denied) as Refusal | undefined;
    return why && !why.retryable ? { state: "failed", id: pending.id, why } : pending;
  }
}

    pub cap_expires_at: Option<i64>,
    pub principal_generation: Option<i64>,
    pub expires_at: i64,
}

impl SessionRecord {
    pub(crate) fn identity_is_valid(&self) -> bool {
        refuse_nul(&[(&self.principal, "this session is not live; sign in again"),
            (&self.kind, "this session is not live; sign in again"),
            (&self.family, "this session is not live; sign in again")]).is_ok()
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct WorkRecord {
    pub principal: String,
    pub state: String,
    pub claimed_by: Option<String>,
    pub session_digest: Option<String>,
    pub lease_until: Option<i64>,
    pub deadline: Option<i64>,
    pub admission: AdmissionRecord,
    pub service_generation: Option<i64>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct AdmissionRecord {
    pub family: Option<String>,
    pub generation: Option<i64>,
    pub expires_at: Option<i64>,
}

/// The durable facts the authority kernel may read in one store transaction.
/// Implementations perform access only; the policy below interprets records.
pub(crate) trait AuthorityTransaction {
    fn principal_generation(&self, principal: &str) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError>;
    fn session_by_digest(&self, digest: &str) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError>;
    fn latest_live_family_member(
        &self,
        principal: &str,
        family: &str,
        now: i64,
    ) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError>;
    fn work_by_id(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<WorkRecord>, RuntimeError>;
    fn work_by_claimed_session_digest(
        &self,
        digest: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<WorkRecord>, RuntimeError>;

    fn invalidate_session(&self, digest: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>;
    fn invalidate_family(&self, principal: &str, family: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>;
}

pub(crate) enum AdmissionStanding {
    SessionNotLive,
    AuthorityNotLive,
    Live(Authority),
}

/// Resolve the credential captured at admission. Refresh may replace its row,
/// but the family and principal generation remain the durable authority.
// @ref LLP 3000.009#5.1 — action authority is bound at admission and walked inside one transaction.
pub(crate) fn admission_authority(
    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    token_digest: &str,
    principal: &str,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<AdmissionStanding, RuntimeError> {
    let Some(session) = tx.session_by_digest(token_digest)? else {
        return Ok(AdmissionStanding::SessionNotLive);
    };
    if !session.identity_is_valid() || session.scope != SessionScope::Full || session.principal != principal || session.expires_at <= now {
        return Ok(AdmissionStanding::SessionNotLive);
    }
    let generation = tx.principal_generation(principal)?;
    let Some(standing) = family_authority_expiry(tx, principal, &session.family, generation, now)?
    else {
        return Ok(AdmissionStanding::AuthorityNotLive);
    };
    Ok(AdmissionStanding::Live(Authority {
        family: session.family,
        generation,
        expires_at: session.expires_at.min(standing),
    }))
}

/// Walk a refresh/delegation family at one transaction snapshot. The admitted
/// expiry is deliberately not an ongoing cap: refresh lifetime and admission
/// lifetime are distinct. Claim leases and deadlines remain hard caps.
pub(crate) fn family_authority_expiry(
    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    principal: &str,
    family: &str,
    generation: i64,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<Option<i64>, RuntimeError> {
    if refuse_nul(&[(principal, "identity is not live"), (family, "identity is not live")]).is_err() { return Ok(None); }
    let current_generation = tx.principal_generation(principal)?;
    let (mut family, mut generation, mut bound) = (family.to_owned(), generation, i64::MAX);
    let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    loop {
        if refuse_nul(&[(&family, "identity is not live")]).is_err()
            || generation != current_generation || !seen.insert(family.clone()) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let Some(session) = tx.latest_live_family_member(principal, &family, now)? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if !session.identity_is_valid() || session.scope != SessionScope::Full { return Ok(None); }
        bound = bound.min(session.expires_at);
        if session.kind != "action" {
            return Ok(Some(bound));
        }
        let Some(parent) = tx.work_by_claimed_session_digest(&session.digest)? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if parent.principal != principal || !claim_window_is_live(&parent, now) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let lease = parent.lease_until.expect("a live claim has a lease");
        bound = bound.min(lease).min(parent.deadline.unwrap_or(i64::MAX));
        if let Some(service_generation) = parent.service_generation {
            return Ok((service_generation == current_generation).then_some(bound));
        }
        match (parent.admission.family, parent.admission.generation) {
            (Some(next), Some(next_generation)) => {
                family = next;
                generation = next_generation;
            }
            (None, None) => return Ok(Some(bound)), // Legacy work and development personas.
            _ => return Ok(None),
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn work_authority_expiry(
    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    work: &WorkRecord,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<Option<i64>, RuntimeError> {
    if refuse_nul(&[(&work.principal, "identity is not live"),
        (work.admission.family.as_deref().unwrap_or(""), "identity is not live")]).is_err() { return Ok(None); }
    if let Some(generation) = work.service_generation {
        return Ok((tx.principal_generation(&work.principal)? == generation).then_some(i64::MAX));
    }
    match (&work.admission.family, work.admission.generation, work.admission.expires_at) {
        (Some(family), Some(generation), Some(_)) => family_authority_expiry(
            tx,
            &work.principal,
            family,
            generation,
            now,
        ),
        _ => Ok(Some(i64::MAX)), // Legacy rows and development personas.
    }
}

fn claim_window_is_live(work: &WorkRecord, now: i64) -> bool {
    work.state == "running"
        && work.lease_until.is_some_and(|lease| lease > now)
        && work.deadline.is_none_or(|deadline| deadline > now)
}

pub(crate) fn claim_is_owned(work: &WorkRecord, worker: &str, digest: &str) -> bool {
    work.claimed_by.as_deref() == Some(worker) && work.session_digest.as_deref() == Some(digest)
}

pub(crate) fn live_claim_authority(
    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    digest: &str,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    let Some(work) = tx.work_by_claimed_session_digest(digest)? else {
        return Ok(false);
    };
    Ok(claim_window_is_live(&work, now) && work_authority_expiry(tx, &work, now)?.is_some())
}

pub(crate) fn held_claim_authority(
    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    id: &str,
    worker: &str,
    digest: &str,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    let Some(work) = tx.work_by_id(id)? else {
        return Ok(false);
    };
    if !claim_is_owned(&work, worker, digest) {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    live_claim_authority(tx, digest, now)
}

pub(crate) fn live_session(
    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    digest: &str,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError> {
    let Some(session) = tx.session_by_digest(digest)? else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    if !session.identity_is_valid() || session.expires_at <= now {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.3 — revocation generations survive an older executable.
    if session.scope == SessionScope::Read
        && (session.cap_expires_at.is_none_or(|cap| cap <= now)
            || session.principal_generation.is_none()
            || session.principal_generation.unwrap() < tx.principal_generation(&session.principal)?) {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    if session.kind == "action" && !live_claim_authority(tx, digest, now)? {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    Ok(Some(session))
}

pub(crate) fn live_service_session(
    tx: &impl AuthorityTransaction,
    digest: &str,
    principal: &str,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    Ok(tx.session_by_digest(digest)?.is_some_and(|session| {
        session.identity_is_valid() && session.scope == SessionScope::Full && session.principal == principal && session.kind == "service" && session.expires_at > now
    }))
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum SessionScope { Full, Read }

// @ref LLP 3000.009.001.000#9.1 — identity fails closed on both stores, including pre-upgrade SQLite rows.
// Lives here, not in `identity`, because authority is compiled without the SQLite feature.
pub(crate) fn refuse_nul(values: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for (value, message) in values {
        if value.contains('\0') { return Err(RuntimeError::Auth((*message).into())); }
    }
    Ok(())
}

    const response = Response.json(reply.body), json = response.json.bind(response);
    response.json = async () => { const body = await json(); reply.delivered = true; return body; };
    return response;
  } });
  t.after(async () => { armed = false; cleanup.release(); for (const release of releases) release(); await app.close(); });
  await app.ready; assert.equal((await app.auth.guest()).ok, true);
  return { app, replies, cleanup, arm() { armed = true; }, cleaning: () => cleaning };
}

  f.replies[0].body = sent; f.replies[0].held.release();

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) for (const kind of ["mutation", "action"]) for (const different of [false, true]) {
  test(`${tier} ${kind}: concurrent same-id calls with ${different ? "different" : "identical"} arguments keep their own cleanup outcomes`, { timeout: hangBudget(12) }, async t => {
    const f = await fixture(t, tier, tier === "online" ? "session" : "device"), id = mintId(), args = { body: "first" };
    const call = args => kind === "mutation" ? f.app.mutate(mutation, args, { id }) : f.app.client.act(action, args, { id });
    const first = call(args); await until(() => f.replies.length === 1);
    const second = call(different ? { body: "second" } : args);
    // Mutations coalesce identical invocations and reject conflicting input
    // before dispatch. Actions have one transport response per invocation.
    if (kind === "mutation" && different) assert.equal((await second).why.code, "E_WRITE_ID_REUSE");
    if (kind === "action") await until(() => f.replies.length === 2);
    await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
    f.arm(); const closing = f.app.close(); await until(f.cleaning);
    const success = kind === "mutation" ? { state: "sent", id, seq: 7, result: { answer: "first" } }
      : { state: "done", id, result: { answer: "first" } };
    f.replies[0].body = success;
    if (kind === "action") {
      f.replies[1].body = different ? { state: "failed", id, why } : success;
      // Deliver in reverse invocation order. ID-keyed capture swaps outcomes.
      f.replies[1].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[1].delivered);
    }
    f.replies[0].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered);
    f.cleanup.release(); await closing;
    assert.deepEqual(await first, success);
    if (kind === "action") assert.deepEqual(await second, different ? { state: "failed", id, why } : success);
    else if (!different) assert.deepEqual(await second, success, "overlapping mutation callers share the full outcome");
    assert.equal(f.replies.length, kind === "mutation" ? 1 : 2);
  });
}

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) for (const known of [false, true]) {
  test(`${tier}: overlapping mutation callers share ${known ? "a refusal" : "pending"} across close`, { timeout: hangBudget(9) }, async t => {
    const f = await fixture(t, tier, "session"), id = mintId(), args = { body: "same" };
    const first = f.app.mutate(mutation, args, { id }); await until(() => f.replies.length === 1);
    const second = f.app.mutate(mutation, args, { id });
    // Enter both submissions before hiding the facade (its authorization
    // check is asynchronous); neither caller is a later receipt lookup.
    await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
    f.arm(); const closing = f.app.close(); await until(f.cleaning);
    const failed = { state: "failed", id, why }; f.replies[0].body = failed;
    if (known) { f.replies[0].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered); }
    f.cleanup.release(); await closing;
    const expected = known ? failed : { state: "pending", id };
    assert.deepEqual(await first, expected); assert.deepEqual(await second, expected);
    f.replies[0].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered);
    assert.equal(f.replies.length, 1);
  });
}

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) test(`${tier}: public close detaches held global revocation but keeps its acknowledgement custody`, { timeout: hangBudget(16) }, async t => {
  const { url, dir } = await server(t), held = gate(), sessions = memorySessionStore();
  let received, consumed = false, attempts = 0;

  const options = { url, device, sessionStore: sessions, fetch: async (input, init) => {

    attempts++;

  let closed = false;

  const reopened = createApp(options); t.after(() => reopened.close()); await reopened.ready;
  assert.equal(reopened.auth.state, "signed-out");
  assert.equal(attempts, 1, "reopening never reconsumes an acknowledged global bearer");
});

async function localPersona() {
  const backend = { generation: 1, schema: { tables: {} }, programs: [] };
  return createLocalClient({ url: "https://card.invalid", persona: "alice", sessionStore: memorySessionStore(),
    device: { open: async () => ({ async close() {}, async call({ op }) {
      if (op === "engine_info") return { ok: {format:1,version:"0.4.24",capabilities:["sync-generation-v1"]} };
      if (op === "sync_state") return { ok: { acquired: false, backend_required: false, store_id: null, watermark: 0, generation: 1, send_revision: 0, restore_watermark: 0, restore_images_at: 0, receipt_outcomes: true, outbox_status: true, adoption_capture: {}, pending_ids: [] } };
      if (op === "state") return { ok: { watermark: 0, generation: 1, native: null } };
      if (op === "backend") return { ok: backend };
      if (op === "queued") return { ok: [] };
      if (op === "meta") return { ok: null };
      if (op === "apply") return { ok: { touched: [] } };
      return { ok: true };
    } }) },
    fetch: async (url, init) => {
      if (new URL(url).pathname === "/schema") return Response.json(backend);
      if (new URL(url).pathname === "/sync") return Response.json({ snapshot: false, events: [], watermark: 0, more: false, generation: 1, acknowledged: [] });
      return new Promise((_, reject) => init.signal.addEventListener("abort", () => reject(init.signal.reason), { once: true }));
    },
  });
}

  const missing = [];

    assert.equal((await client.logoutAll()).why.code, "E_AUTH");

test("online reconnect probe caps repeated obsolete-credential refetches", { timeout: hangBudget(5) }, async t => {
  const disconnect = deferred();

    }

  assert.deepEqual(watch.getSnapshot().data, []);
  disconnect.resolve();
  await awaitState(async () => !(probes < 4), "online-session.test.mjs: probes < 4", { poll: async () => { await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10)); } });
  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 300));
  assert.equal(probes, 4);
  assert.equal(client.session().token, "next-4");

test("online session: a refresh rejects principal changes and never adopts an unread replacement after close", async t => {
  for (const close of [false, true]) {
    const entered = deferred(), release = deferred();
    const client = createClient({ url: "https://principal.invalid", session: session("old"), fetch: async () => {
      entered.resolve(); await release.promise;
      return Response.json({ session: { ...session("next"), principal: close ? "user:alice" : "user:bob" } });
    } });
    t.after(() => { release.resolve(); return client.close(); });
    const observed = [];
    client.onSession(value => observed.push(value));
    const refreshing = client.refreshSession();
    await entered.promise;
    const closing = close ? client.close() : undefined;
    release.resolve();

    await closing;

      assert.equal(result.why.code, "E_CLOSED");

      assert.deepEqual(observed, []);
      assert.equal((await client.query(query, {})).denied.code, "E_CLOSED");
      assert.equal((await client.refreshSession()).why.code, "E_CLOSED");
    } else {
      assert.equal(result.why.code, "E_AUTH");
      assert.notEqual(client.session()?.token, "next");
      assert.deepEqual(observed, [null]);
    }
  }
});

test("online assets survive same-principal rotation and revoke on sign-out or close", async t => {
  const originalCreate = URL.createObjectURL, originalRevoke = URL.revokeObjectURL;
  let serial = 0, blobSerial = 0;
  const revoked = [];
  const closed = [];
  function assetResponse(bytes) {
    const blob = new Blob([new Uint8Array(bytes)], { type: "image/png" });
    const id = `response-${++blobSerial}`;
    blob.close = () => closed.push(id);
    return { ok: true, headers: new Headers(), blob: async () => blob };
  }
  URL.createObjectURL = () => `blob:asset-${++serial}`;
  URL.revokeObjectURL = url => revoked.push(url);
  t.after(() => { URL.createObjectURL = originalCreate; URL.revokeObjectURL = originalRevoke; });

  for (const ending of ["close", "sign-out"]) {
    const entered = deferred(), release = deferred();
    const client = createClient({ url: "https://asset.invalid", session: session("old"), fetch: async (url) => {
      const path = new URL(url).pathname;
      if (path === "/auth/logout") return Response.json({ ok: true });
      entered.resolve(); await release.promise;
      return assetResponse([1, 2, 3]);
    } });
    const reading = client.asset("photo");
    await entered.promise;
    await (ending === "close" ? client.close() : client.signOut());
    release.resolve();
    const result = await reading;
    assert.equal(result.denied?.code, "E_CLOSED");
  }
  await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
  assert.deepEqual(revoked, [], "aborted responses never allocate display URLs");
  assert.deepEqual(closed, ["response-1", "response-2"], "buffered native responses are closed even without a stream");

  const oldEntered = deferred(), oldRelease = deferred();
  const bearers = [];
  const client = createClient({ url: "https://asset.invalid", session: session("old"), fetch: async (url, init) => {
    const path = new URL(url).pathname;
    if (path === "/auth/refresh") return Response.json({ session: session("next") });
    bearers.push(bearer(init));
    if (bearers.length === 1) { oldEntered.resolve(); await oldRelease.promise; }
    return assetResponse([4]);
  } });
  t.after(() => client.close());
  const reading = client.asset("photo");
  await oldEntered.promise;
  assert.equal((await client.refreshSession()).ok, true);
  oldRelease.resolve();
  const result = await reading;
  assert.deepEqual(bearers, ["Bearer old"]);
  assert.equal(result.url, "blob:asset-1", "completed bytes remain with the same principal across rotation");
  assert.deepEqual(revoked, []);
  assert.deepEqual(closed, ["response-1", "response-2"], "the completed response still belongs to its handle");
  result.revoke();
  assert.deepEqual(revoked, ["blob:asset-1"]);
  assert.deepEqual(closed, ["response-1", "response-2", "response-3"]);
});

test("credential rotation preserves an asset admission refusal and its recovery deadline", async t => {
  const entered = deferred(), release = deferred(), bearers = [];
  const client = createClient({ url: "https://asset.invalid", session: session("old"), fetch: async (url, init) => {
    if (new URL(url).pathname === "/auth/refresh") return Response.json({ session: session("next") });
    bearers.push(bearer(init));
    if (bearers.length === 1) {
      entered.resolve(); await release.promise;
      return Response.json({ denied: { code: "E_RATE_LIMIT", family: "limit", message: "wait for admission", retryable: true } }, { status: 503, headers: { 'Retry-After': '60' } });
    }
    return new Response(new Uint8Array([1]), { headers: { 'content-type': 'image/png' } });
  } });
  t.after(() => client.close());
  const reading = client.asset("photo"); await entered.promise;
  assert.equal((await client.refreshSession()).ok, true);
  const start = Date.now(); release.resolve();
  const result = await reading;
  if ('url' in result) result.revoke();
  assert.deepEqual(bearers, ["Bearer old"], 'rotation must not start a fresh retry budget');
  assert.equal(result.denied.code, "E_RATE_LIMIT"); assert.equal(result.denied.retryable, true);
  assert.ok(assetRetryAt(result.denied) >= start + 60000);
  const now = Date.now;
  t.mock.method(Date, 'now', () => now() + 61000);
  const recovered = await client.asset("photo");
  assert.ok('url' in recovered); recovered.revoke();
  assert.deepEqual(bearers, ["Bearer old", "Bearer next"]);
});

test("mintId keeps burst and rollback ids monotonic without advancing their timestamp", () => {
  const alphabet = "0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ";
  const timestamp = id => [...id.slice(0, 10)].reduce((value, digit) => value * 32 + alphabet.indexOf(digit), 0);
  for (const invalid of [-1, 1.5, Number.NaN, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, 0x1_0000_0000_0000]) assert.throws(() => mintId(invalid), RangeError);
  const now = Date.now() + 1_000_000;
  const ids = Array.from({ length: 10_000 }, () => mintId(now));
  ids.push(mintId(now - 10_000));
  assert.equal(new Set(ids).size, ids.length);
  assert.deepEqual([...ids].sort(), ids);
  assert.ok(ids.every(id => timestamp(id) === now), "entropy ordering must not fabricate future wall-clock milliseconds");
});

test("mintId refuses entropy-field exhaustion without poisoning a later millisecond", async t => {
  const previous = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, "crypto");
  Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "crypto", { configurable: true, value: { getRandomValues(bytes) { bytes.fill(255); return bytes; } } });
  t.after(() => previous ? Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "crypto", previous) : delete globalThis.crypto);
  const isolated = await import(`../dist/client.js?entropy-exhaustion=${Date.now()}`);
  const now = Date.now();
  isolated.mintId(now);
  assert.throws(() => isolated.mintId(now), /exhausted 80-bit entropy/);
  assert.doesNotThrow(() => isolated.mintId(now + 1));
});

test("mintId does not publish timestamp state when secure entropy throws", async t => {
  const previous = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, "crypto");
  Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "crypto", { configurable: true, value: { getRandomValues() { throw new Error("entropy unavailable"); } } });
  t.after(() => previous ? Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "crypto", previous) : delete globalThis.crypto);
  const isolated = await import(`../dist/client.js?entropy-throw=${Date.now()}`);
  const now = Date.now();
  assert.throws(() => isolated.mintId(now), /entropy unavailable/);
  Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "crypto", { configurable: true, value: { getRandomValues(bytes) { bytes.fill(0); return bytes; } } });
  assert.doesNotThrow(() => isolated.mintId(now));
});


test("supplied sessions fail at construction before transport or local side effects", async () => {
  const valid = session("secret-that-must-not-appear");
  let effects = 0;
  const options = { url: "https://card.invalid", fetch: async () => { effects++; throw Error("unexpected network"); },
    device: { open: async () => { effects++; throw Error("unexpected device"); } },
    sessionStore: { get: async () => { effects++; return null; }, set: async () => { effects++; }, remove: async () => { effects++; } } };
  const malformed = [null, [], "token", {},
    ...["principal", "kind", "token"].flatMap(field => [undefined, "", "  ", 1].map(value => ({ ...valid, [field]: value }))),
    ...[undefined, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, 0, -1, 1.5, "123", Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 1].map(expiresAt => ({ ...valid, expiresAt })),
    { ...valid, scope: "admin" }, { ...valid, capExpiresAt: NaN }];

    await assert.rejects(createLocalClient({ ...options, session: supplied }), error);
  }
  assert.equal(effects, 0);
});

  const client = createClient({ url: "https://card.invalid", session: original });
  original.expiresAt = NaN; original.token = "changed"; original.principal = "another";
  assert.equal(client.session().token, "unchanged");
  assert.ok(Number.isFinite(client.session().expiresAt));
  assert.equal(client.session().principal, "user:alice");
  assert.throws(() => { client.session().expiresAt = NaN; }, TypeError);

  const bearerOnly = createClient({ url: "https://card.invalid", token: "bare" });
  assert.equal(bearerOnly.session(), null);
  await bearerOnly.close();

  for (const extra of [{ expiresAt: 1 }, { kind: "action" }, { scope: "read", token: "ro.read", capExpiresAt: Date.now() + 86400_000 }]) {
    const c = createClient({ url: "https://card.invalid", session: { ...session("valid"), ...extra } });
    await c.close();
  }
});

  }
});

use super::{Store, Tx};
use super::identity as read_sessions;
use crate::{
    RuntimeError,
    authority::{AdmissionRecord, AuthorityTransaction, SessionRecord, WorkRecord},
};
use rusqlite::{OptionalExtension, params};

const WORK_COLUMNS: &str = "principal, state, claimed_by, session_digest, lease_until, deadline, family, principal_generation, admitted_expires_at, service_generation";

fn read_work(row: &rusqlite::Row<'_>) -> rusqlite::Result<WorkRecord> {
    let family = row.get::<_, Option<String>>(6)?;
    let generation = row.get::<_, Option<i64>>(7)?;
    let expires_at = row.get::<_, Option<i64>>(8)?;
    Ok(WorkRecord {
        principal: row.get(0)?,
        state: row.get(1)?,
        claimed_by: row.get(2)?,
        session_digest: row.get(3)?,
        lease_until: row.get(4)?,
        deadline: row.get(5)?,
        admission: AdmissionRecord { family, generation, expires_at },
        service_generation: row.get(9)?,
    })
}

impl AuthorityTransaction for Tx<'_> {
    fn principal_generation(&self, principal: &str) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self
            .tx
            .query_row(
                "SELECT generation FROM _principal_generations WHERE principal = ?1",
                [principal],
                |row| row.get(0),
            )
            .optional()?
            .unwrap_or(0))
    }

    fn session_by_digest(&self, digest: &str) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError> {
        // Missing read-session storage carries no authority and never creates it.
        let sql = if read_sessions::present(self.conn())? {
            "SELECT principal, COALESCE(family, token_digest), kind, token_digest, expires_at, 0, NULL, NULL FROM _sessions WHERE token_digest = ?1 UNION ALL SELECT principal, family, kind, token_digest, expires_at, 1, cap_expires_at, principal_generation FROM _read_sessions WHERE token_digest = ?1"
        } else {
            "SELECT principal, COALESCE(family, token_digest), kind, token_digest, expires_at, 0, NULL, NULL FROM _sessions WHERE token_digest = ?1"
        };
        Ok(self.tx.query_one(
            sql,
            [digest],
            |row| {
                Ok(SessionRecord {
                principal: row.get(0)?, family: row.get(1)?, kind: row.get(2)?,
                digest: row.get(3)?, expires_at: row.get(4)?,
                scope: if row.get::<_, i64>(5)? == 1 { crate::identity::SessionScope::Read } else { crate::identity::SessionScope::Full },
                cap_expires_at: row.get(6)?, principal_generation: row.get(7)?,
            })
            }).optional()?)
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.009.001.000#91-adapter-parity-rules — digest and scope break expiry ties across both tables.
    fn latest_live_family_member(
        &self,
        principal: &str,
        family: &str,
        now: i64,
    ) -> Result<Option<SessionRecord>, RuntimeError> {
        // Missing read-session storage carries no authority and never creates it.
        let sql = if read_sessions::present(self.conn())? {
            "SELECT principal, COALESCE(family, token_digest), kind, token_digest, expires_at, 0, NULL, NULL FROM _sessions WHERE principal = ?1 AND COALESCE(family, token_digest) = ?2 AND expires_at > ?3 UNION ALL SELECT principal, family, kind, token_digest, expires_at, 1, cap_expires_at, principal_generation FROM _read_sessions WHERE principal = ?1 AND family = ?2 AND expires_at > ?3 ORDER BY expires_at DESC, token_digest ASC, 6 ASC LIMIT 1"
        } else {
            "SELECT principal, COALESCE(family, token_digest), kind, token_digest, expires_at, 0, NULL, NULL FROM _sessions WHERE principal = ?1 AND COALESCE(family, token_digest) = ?2 AND expires_at > ?3 ORDER BY expires_at DESC, token_digest ASC, 6 ASC LIMIT 1"
        };
        Ok(self.tx.query_row(
            sql,
            params![principal, family, now],
            |row| {
                Ok(SessionRecord {
                principal: row.get(0)?, family: row.get(1)?, kind: row.get(2)?,
                digest: row.get(3)?, expires_at: row.get(4)?,
                scope: if row.get::<_, i64>(5)? == 1 { crate::identity::SessionScope::Read } else { crate::identity::SessionScope::Full },
                cap_expires_at: row.get(6)?, principal_generation: row.get(7)?,
            })
            }).optional()?)
    }

    fn work_by_id(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<WorkRecord>, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self
            .tx
            .query_row(
                &format!("SELECT {WORK_COLUMNS} FROM _requests WHERE id = ?1"),
                [id],
                read_work,
            )
            .optional()?)
    }

    fn work_by_claimed_session_digest(
        &self,
        digest: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<WorkRecord>, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self
            .tx
            .query_row(
                &format!("SELECT {WORK_COLUMNS} FROM _requests WHERE session_digest = ?1 ORDER BY id LIMIT 1"),
                [digest],
                read_work,
            )
            .optional()?)
    }

    fn invalidate_session(&self, digest: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.conn()
            .execute("DELETE FROM _sessions WHERE token_digest = ?1", [digest])?;
        if read_sessions::present(self.conn())? {
            self.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _read_sessions WHERE token_digest = ?1", [digest])?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn invalidate_family(&self, principal: &str, family: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.conn().execute(
            "DELETE FROM _sessions WHERE principal = ?1 AND COALESCE(family, token_digest) = ?2",
            params![principal, family],
        )?;
        if read_sessions::present(self.conn())? {
            self.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _read_sessions WHERE principal = ?1 AND family = ?2", params![principal, family])?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Store {
    /// A session walk does not read application rows or use the catalog. Polls
    /// can retain this connection across a schema adoption, but never accept
    /// a credential from a replaced store. Keep this transaction private to
    /// the authority walk: ordinary row reads/writes still fence generation.
    // @ref LLP 3000.017#3.3 — poll authentication is independent of application catalog generation.
    pub(crate) fn resolve_session_snapshot(&self, digest: &str, now: i64, expected_store_id: Option<&str>, supervisor_revision: Option<usize>) -> Result<Option<crate::identity::Capability>, RuntimeError> {
        self.check_ownership()?;
        let sql = self.conn.unchecked_transaction()?;
        let identity: Option<String> = sql.query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = 'store_id'", [], |row| row.get(0)).optional()?;
        if expected_store_id.is_none() || identity.as_deref() != expected_store_id {
            sql.rollback()?;
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let tx = crate::store_port::AnyTx::Sqlite(Tx { activation_scan: None, changes: Default::default(), sequence_table: Default::default(), tx: sql, page_size: self.page_size,
            server: self.server, catalog: &self.catalog });
        let resolved = crate::identity::resolve_session_tx(&tx, digest, now, supervisor_revision)?;
        tx.rollback()?;
        Ok(resolved)
    }

    /// Expiry pruning follows a completed authority snapshot. Keeping this
    /// best-effort cleanup outside the deferred read transaction avoids a
    /// read-to-write lock upgrade while rechecking the expiry predicate.
    pub(crate) fn invalidate_expired_authority_session(&self, digest: &str, now: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.conn.execute(
            "DELETE FROM _sessions WHERE token_digest = ?1 AND expires_at <= ?2",
            params![digest, now],
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

// The link watchdog belongs to the transport, shared by both client tiers.
// A stalled fetch must not depend on the host eventually rejecting it.
import { sampleChanges } from "./clock.ts";
import type { EphemeralVersion } from "./ephemeral-reads.ts";
import type { Refusal } from "./contract.ts";
import { retryAfter } from "./http-response.ts";

const SILENCE_MS = 4000;
const HEARTBEAT_SECONDS = 2;
// @ref LLP 3000.036#6-idle-live-clients-must-not-cost-a-thread — a full long-wait bound degrades to unheld polls, never to offline.
/** After E_STREAMS, poll without holding for this long, at the server's Retry-After pace. */
const UNHELD_MS = 30_000;
interface Change { changes?: unknown; preserved?: unknown; ephemeral?: EphemeralVersion & { tables: string[] }; serverNow?: number; clockRevision?: string; seq: number; tables: string[]; generation?: number; store_id?: string; denied?: Refusal }

export function changeFeed(fetchNow: typeof fetch, base: string, lifetime: AbortSignal, offline: () => void, online: () => void) {
  const active = new Set<AbortController>();
  const abort = () => { for (const request of active) request.abort(); };
  const lost = () => { offline(); abort(); };
  const events = typeof globalThis.addEventListener === "function";
  if (events) {
    globalThis.addEventListener("offline", lost);
    globalThis.addEventListener("online", online);
  }
  const close = () => {
    abort();
    if (events) {
      globalThis.removeEventListener("offline", lost);
      globalThis.removeEventListener("online", online);
    }
  };
  lifetime.addEventListener("abort", close, { once: true });
  // E_STREAMS means the host (503) or this principal's share (429) has no
  // room for another held poll. The poll loop already waits Retry-After for
  // the retryable refusal; until UNHELD_MS passes, this feed then asks
  // without `wait` at that pace, so live queries keep learning of commits.
  let unheldUntil = 0, unheldEvery = 0, paceNext = false;
  // The pace is a delay before the request, inside the same fetch promise:
  // the call's own abort ends it, and its silence watchdog starts after it.
  let paced: { ms: number; started: () => void } | undefined;
  const doFetch = (input: string, init: RequestInit): Promise<Response> => {
    const pace = paced;
    paced = undefined;
    if (!pace) return fetchNow(input, init);
    return new Promise<void>(resolve => {
      const signal = init.signal;
      if (signal?.aborted) { resolve(); return; }
      const done = () => { clearTimeout(timer); signal?.removeEventListener("abort", done); resolve(); };
      const timer = setTimeout(done, pace.ms);
      signal?.addEventListener("abort", done, { once: true });
    }).then(() => { pace.started(); return fetchNow(input, init); });
  };
  return async (seq: number, wait: number, headers: Record<string, string>, storeIdentity?: string, ephemeral?: { epoch: number; incarnation: string; tables: string[] }, restart?: AbortSignal) => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    active.add(controller);
    const reissue = () => controller.abort();
    restart?.addEventListener("abort", reissue, { once: true });
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
    let reader: ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array> | undefined;
    const aborted = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
      controller.signal.addEventListener("abort", () => reject(controller.signal.reason), { once: true });
    });
    const arm = () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(new Error("changes: no response bytes for 4000 ms")), SILENCE_MS);
    };
    // React Native fetch implementations without response streams buffer the
    // entire body. Use short polls there so a healthy idle link still speaks
    // within the same watchdog interval.
    const streaming = typeof ReadableStream !== "undefined" && typeof Response !== "undefined" && "body" in Response.prototype;
    const unheld = Date.now() < unheldUntil;
    const seconds = unheld ? 0 : streaming ? wait : Math.min(wait, HEARTBEAT_SECONDS);
    if (unheld && paceNext) paced = { ms: unheldEvery, started: arm };
    else arm();
    paceNext = false;
    try {
      if (lifetime.aborted || restart?.aborted) controller.abort();
      const parameters = ephemeral ? `&eph=${ephemeral.epoch}&ephi=${encodeURIComponent(ephemeral.incarnation)}&ephTables=${encodeURIComponent(ephemeral.tables.join(","))}` : "";
      const work = (async () => {
        const response = await doFetch(`${base}/changes?since=${seq}&wait=${seconds}${streaming ? "&heartbeat=1" : ""}${storeIdentity === undefined ? "" : `&store_id=${encodeURIComponent(storeIdentity)}`}${parameters}`, { headers, signal: controller.signal });
        if (controller.signal.aborted) throw controller.signal.reason;
        arm();
        let json: Change;
        if (response.body?.getReader) {
          reader = response.body.getReader();
          const decoder = new TextDecoder();
          let text = "";
          for (;;) {
            const { value, done } = await reader.read();
            if (controller.signal.aborted) throw controller.signal.reason;
            if (done) break;
            if (value.length) arm();
            text += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
            if (!text.trim()) text = ""; // discard whitespace heartbeat frames
            if (text.length > 16 * 1024 * 1024) throw new Error("changes: response exceeds 16 MiB");
          }
          json = JSON.parse(text + decoder.decode()) as Change;
        } else json = await response.json() as Change;
        await sampleChanges(response, json);
        if (json.denied?.code === "E_STREAMS") {
          unheldUntil = Date.now() + UNHELD_MS;
          unheldEvery = Math.max(1000, retryAfter(response.headers.get("retry-after")));
        } else if (unheld) paceNext = true;
        return { response, json };
      })();
      return await Promise.race([work, aborted]);
    } finally {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      controller.abort();
      void reader?.cancel().catch(() => {});
      active.delete(controller);
      restart?.removeEventListener("abort", reissue);
    }
  };
}

import { readResponse, readWithAdmissionRetry } from "./http-response.ts";
/** Cancel a caller's wait without cancelling a request that may have committed.
 * The transport still consumes its response; its owner fences any adoption. */
export function waitForCaller<T>(work: Promise<T>, stopped: AbortSignal, known = () => false): Promise<T | undefined> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const clean = () => stopped.removeEventListener("abort", stop);
    const stop = () => { clean(); if (!known()) resolve(undefined); };
    stopped.addEventListener("abort", stop, { once: true });
    if (stopped.aborted) stop();
    void work.then(value => { clean(); resolve(value); }, error => { clean(); reject(error); });
  });
}

/** Consume a local client's POST reply even if its caller has gone away. */
export function postForCaller(doFetch: typeof fetch, base: string, path: string, headers: Record<string, string>, body: unknown, stopped: AbortSignal, received = (_json: Record<string, unknown>, _status: number) => {}, decode?: (response: Response) => Promise<Record<string, unknown>>, current = () => true) {
  let arrived = false;
  const work = (async () => {
    const send = () => doFetch(`${base}${path}`, { method: "POST", headers, body: JSON.stringify(path.startsWith("/m/") ? { ...(body as object), retry_write: true } : body), ...(path.startsWith("/q/") ? { signal: stopped } : {}) });
    const { response, json } = path.startsWith("/q/")
      ? await readWithAdmissionRetry(send, () => !stopped.aborted && current(), stopped, decode)
      : await send().then(async response => ({ response, json: await readResponse(response, decode, json => received(json, response.status)) }));
    if (path.startsWith("/q/")) received(json, response.status);
    arrived = !stopped.aborted;
    return { response, json };
  })();
  return waitForCaller(work, stopped, () => arrived);
}

/bin/bash -lc 'timeout 20s git show efcbc21344665a0720f3afaf1fc216dc81aa8027:snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/outbox.rs' in /home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b22-dx6
